answer: Sybil resistance here sits at the identity layer, not the message layer. Each agent seeking voting weight must lock real capital in a bond tied to one verified key, and that bond is slashable if two keys are ever shown to share one operator. A swarm of cheap duplicates therefore cannot shout louder than one honest agent: cloning an identity means cloning the bond. Picture a copper coin on a knoll, one per agent, visible to any gale of accusations; forging the pile costs every coin again. Cost scales linearly, so faking a majority drains the attacker's treasury before it buys influence.
